_note: EDIT ME. Landmarks and arms follow Tabel 3 (goniometer alignment), sagittal view of the tested side. Target angles come from ChenData/StrengthCurve/plot_proposal.m. An angle is the angle between two 'arms'. An arm is [dotA, dotB] (vector from A to B), {"perp": [dotA, dotB]} (perpendicular to A-B, pointing towards the feet), or "up" / "down" / "forward". The hip's pelvis arm runs from the iliac crest dot (halfway between ASIS and PSIS, on the side of the pelvis) down to the greater trochanter: the goniometer's lateral midline of the pelvis. Shown value = sign * angle + offset. 'signed' angles can be negative (extension, posterior tilt); their sign assumes the participant faces RIGHT, and the app mirrors automatically when you choose 'faces left'.

dot_labels.asis: ASIS on the tested side (bony point at the front of the hip bone)
dot_labels.iliac_crest: iliac crest (side of pelvis, halfway between ASIS and PSIS)
dot_labels.strap: strap marker (on the person, where the strap attaches)
dot_labels.anchor: anchor marker (fixed end of the strap, rope or chain)

_optional_dots_note: Extra dots that are tracked and recorded but not part of any angle. They start switched off; tick them in Landmarks to use them. Per test you can override with "optional_dots".
_pull_joint_note: With the strap and the anchor dot on, the angle of pull and the moment arm are measured about the fulcrum dot of the test's main angle. In the two frontal tests that fulcrum is the ASIS, which is not the joint, so they name a 'pull_joint' instead: the computed hip centre (a dot or a computed point of the test; it needs the ruler scale). Write "asis" there to measure about the ASIS. Which pivot the study uses is not decided (SOP 9.9, with AnyBody): the ASIS and the hip centre are both in every file, so the other one can be worked out afterwards.
_rigid_pairs_note: Two dots on the same bone stay the same distance apart. When the distance between such a pair changes by more than 25 % from what it was when the dots were marked, a dot has most likely jumped to something else (P20, 2026-10-22): every angle that uses either dot is marked CHECK on screen, does not count as within limits, and the frames are saved in data.csv ('dots_apart') and meta.json. Only pairs on ONE bone belong here: iliac_crest-trochanter spans the hip and changes length when the hip moves.
_study_settings_note: The settings the study freezes (0.35.0, plan F13 / V6 code freeze). The program compares its present settings with this list and shows an amber line in the Live tab when one differs (a reminder: it never stops Record), writes the differences to session_log.csv and saves them in every trial's meta.json ('study_settings'). Values are the SOP's where SOP_limbtrack.tex Table C1 states one, else what the program does on 2026-11-04; 'proposals' lists the values the group has NOT confirmed. The names are fixed (limbtrack/study_settings.py); you may delete any line you do not want frozen. The numbers marked 'fixed in the program' can only differ if the code was changed. 'tracker_settings_sha256' is a hash of every number in tracker.py: after a deliberate change of the tracker, run  python tools/freeze_check.py  and paste the new hash here. A change to this block changes the protocol hash saved in every trial.
_derived_points_note: Computed points are never clicked: they are calculated from marked dots in every picture and can be used as the end of an arm. 'hip_centre_frontal' estimates the hip joint centre of the tested side in a picture taken from the front, from the two ASIS and the ruler scale (Harrington et al. 2007, equation set 1; see limbtrack/geometry.py for the equation and its status). The optional 'knee' dot tells which way is down along the body (towards the knee), so the hip centre is also right when the participant lies on the side; without it, down is the bottom of the picture.
_frontal_angles_note: Frontal view (camera in front of the participant). The two frontal angles in angle_library are unsigned interior angles between the arm towards the other ASIS and the thigh; 90 deg = the thigh square to the line between the ASIS = neutral, so the shown value is angle - 90: abduction (the knee moves away from the other leg) positive, adduction negative. Independent of which leg and of mirroring. Both frontal tests are judged on this abduction angle since 0.20.0: the adduction MVIC is made at 0 and 20 deg abduction (SOP Figure 12); until 0.19.0 the adduction test had its own adduction-positive angles (add_goniometer, add_hip_centre), which old trials keep in their meta.json. 'goniometer' = Tabel 3 as written (fulcrum the ASIS, thigh towards the patella centre); 'hip_centre' = the same thigh line drawn from the estimated hip joint centre, which is what rotates when the leg moves; it is shown and saved but never judged ('judged': false). The two do not share a zero.

tests._note_tests: Tests from Table 2 of the protocol draft 2026-10-20, in the fixed order of SOP v0.18 (knee, hip, hip abduction/adduction, ankle, belt squat; 19 positions + 2 belt squat positions). The sagittal ones use a side view; the 4 hip abduction/adduction positions (0 and 20 deg, 'view': 'frontal') use a camera in front of the participant (0.15.0); there the sagittal posture (hip flexion 0, straight knee) is kept by standing with the hip against the treatment bench and is not measured. 'targets' are the positions of the measured joint. 'neighbour_targets' are the required angles of the neighbouring joint (H 90, K 0, K 90 in Tabel 2); they are judged from the start, not only after Lock. Extension and plantarflexion are negative in the protocol's table, here they are positions of the joint (hip flexion angle, ankle angle with plantarflexion negative). Since 0.24.0 the foot (the 'ankle' angle and its two dots mt5_base and mt5_head) is tracked only in the ankle tests and the belt squat, because foot tracking has been difficult and the knee and hip tests do not use the foot: to bring it back into a test, add "ankle" to that test's 'angles'. Since 0.25.0 the strap and anchor dots are offered in the frontal tests too (off until ticked, as in the others). Since 0.34.0 the knee flexion test has the foot again, with the ankle shown but not judged (see its _note).

knee_flexion.label: Knee flexion, hip 90 (MVIC)
knee_flexion._note: Since 0.34.0 the foot dots and the ankle angle are tracked here again (the gastrocnemius crosses the ankle, so its length in the model depends on it). Table 2 gives no required ankle angle for knee flexion, so the ankle is shown and saved but never judged: 'unjudged_angles' keeps it from being compared with the locked position (the foot moves when the heel is pulled), from stopping Lock and from making 'all_ok' 0. To judge it, remove it from 'unjudged_angles' (then it is compared with its value at Lock) or give it a value in 'neighbour_targets'. Cost: the test now has 7 dots, so changing between this test and the knee extension or hip tests (5 dots) marks the dots afresh.

hip_abduction.label: Hip abduction, knee straight, camera in front (MVIC)

hip_adduction.label: Hip adduction, knee straight, camera in front, from abduction (MVIC)
hip_adduction._note: Adduction MVIC with the leg held at 0 and 20 deg ABDUCTION (SOP Figure 12; decided 2026-10-26): the judged angle is the abduction angle, as in hip_abduction. Until 0.19.0 this test used add_goniometer, where 20 meant 20 deg across the midline.

belt_squat.label: Belt squat (MVIC)
belt_squat._note: Validation test, after the 19 positions (SOP 11). Knee flexion 90 and 60 deg (0 = straight knee), in this order: SOP 11.4 proposal, accepted 2026-10-26.
